question.problem: Consider the curve  $r(t)=(6t-6)\,i+4(t-1)^{3/2}\,j+2\,k,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=4{t}^{3/2}.$ Given that $R(s)$ is the parameterization of the given curve by its arc length $s,$ what is the $x$-component of $R?$
question.worked_solution:
First, since  $s=4{t}^{3/2}$,  we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}s & =4{t}^{3/2} \\ {t}^{3/2} & =\frac{s}{4} \\ t & ={(\frac{s}{4})}^{2/3}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The vector function that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r({(\frac{s}{4})}^{2/3}) \\  & =[6{(\frac{s}{4})}^{2/3}-6]\,i+4{[{(\frac{s}{4})}^{2/3}-1]}^{3/2}\,j+2\,k \\  & =6[{(\frac{s}{4})}^{2/3}-1]\,i+4{[{(\frac{s}{4})}^{2/3}-1]}^{3/2}\,j+2\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, the $x$-component of $R$ is

$$
6[{(\frac{s}{4})}^{2/3}-1].
$$
